title: Automated rock joint trace mapping using a supervised learning model trained on synthetic data generated by parametric modelling
mechanism: Parametric (discrete fracture network) synthesis of thin joint traces for segmentation. Mixed training helps when real labels are consistent; pretrain-then-fine-tune is more robust when real labels are noisy or biased.
adaptation: Design rule for any EL crack synthesizer (D06/D33): our crack labels are noisy and source-biased, so compare synthetic pretraining + real fine-tune against mixing synthetic into real batches.
min_experiment: Arm A: house pretrained on synthetic cracks then fine-tuned; Arm B: synthetic mixed at 25%. Baseline: house. Metrics: test crack IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill: neither arm beats house by 0.012 crack IoU or 0.02 E1 relF1@2.
evidence: R: synthetic data supports joint trace detection when real data is scarce; zero-shot from synthetic alone is limited; fine-tuning is robust to noisy labels (qualitative and quantitative, abstract only).
prior_overlap: none. Synthetic crack rendering was not tried; copy-paste is a different mechanism.
